content.page_title: Avoiding overuse of diagnostic tests for pulmonary embolism; D-dimer testing

sections.4.3: Avoiding overuse of diagnostic tests for pulmonary embolism

proportion_confirmed_PE_by_probability.note: Direct prospective comparisons showed similar diagnostic performance between classification rules.

PERC_rule.purpose: Select emergency department patients whose likelihood of PE is so low diagnostic workup should not be initiated
PERC_rule.validation: Prospective validation and a randomized non-inferiority management study suggested safe exclusion of PE in patients with low clinical probability who met all PERC criteria, but low overall prevalence in those studies limits generalizability.

D-dimer_testing_summary.mechanism: D-dimer levels elevated in plasma with acute thrombosis due to activation of coagulation and fibrinolysis

diagnostic_role.negative_predictive_value: High — a normal D-dimer makes acute PE or DVT unlikely
diagnostic_role.positive_predictive_value: Low — elevated D-dimer is not useful for confirming PE

assay_notes.recommended_awareness: Clinicians should be aware of diagnostic performance of the specific D-dimer assay used locally
assay_notes.ELISA_performance: Quantitative ELISA or ELISA-derived assays have diagnostic sensitivity of approximately 95% and can be used to exclude PE in low or intermediate pre-test probability patients
assay_notes.clinical_use: In emergency department, a negative ELISA D-dimer combined with clinical probability can exclude disease without further testing in a substantial proportion of patients with suspected PE
assay_notes.outcome_data: Outcome studies showed 3-month thrombo-embolic risk <1% in patients with low or intermediate clinical probability who were left untreated on the basis of a negative test
